subject.title: [Security] Unsanitized environment variable injection via plugin custom setup scripts

question: Does the plugin installation threat model treat registry/plugin manifest defaults as untrusted data that must never reach a shell interpreter, independently of a plugin package's normal executable-code privileges?
rationale: The appropriate repair depends on the intended plugin trust boundary and whether setup hooks are a supported execution contract; source-level validation alone cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Validate the reported boundary
options.body: Have a security owner reproduce the claimed manifest-to-shell path and land a narrow escaping or process-environment fix if it exists.

options.title: Document the executable-plugin boundary
options.body: If plugin manifests and setup hooks are intentionally equivalent to executable plugin code, document that boundary and close only after confirming no lower-trust registry metadata path exists.

recommendation.title: Validate the reported boundary
recommendation.body: Have a security owner reproduce the claimed manifest-to-shell path and land a narrow escaping or process-environment fix if it exists.

likelyOwner.reason: No evidence-backed individual ownership trail could be established in this review.
